name: brain tumours overview
title: Suspected brain tumour: progressive symptoms and raised intracranial pressure prompt a contrast MRI; metastasis is treated by resection and radiation, a glioma by its grade (an enhancing high-grade glioma is treated at once, a non-enhancing low-grade glioma can be watched) and then its biomarkers set the prognosis, and primary CNS lymphoma is suspected in the immunosuppressed; further columns cover mass effect (raised pressure, then herniation) and paraneoplastic syndromes, the remote immune effects of cancer

root.title: Could it be a brain TUMOUR? The red flag is PROGRESSIVE symptoms
lines: • neuro symptoms or signs progressing over days to weeks · SHORT history (weeks to a few months) = highly malignant · LONG (months or more) = benign or slow-growing
• raised pressure: ↓ consciousness · headache, nausea, vomiting · Cushing response · papilledema (LATE) · herniation
• headache: persistent, progressive, worse lying down and in the morning, wakes from sleep, worse with cough or Valsalva
• focal deficit (weakness, sensory loss, dysphasia, gait, vision), insidious · mental status change: apathy, personality change (mistaken for depression or dementia) · seizures, especially FOCAL
• diagnosis: history · exam · CONTRAST MRI (gadolinium) = test of choice · CT only WITH contrast · TISSUE diagnosis (biopsy or resection) still needed
• steroids for brain swelling · anti-seizure drugs only once there is a seizure · seizure → no driving, Ministry of Transportation notified

groups.title: PRIMARY
lines: gliomas are the most common primary

tiers.title: Glioma: does it ENHANCE with contrast?

head: h
Brain metastasis
most common CNS tumour
15% of cancer deaths: brain mets at autopsy
15-20% of cancers PRESENT as a brain met
pres: • lung: 16% of brain mets (small cell, adenocarcinoma)
progressive positional headache, confusion, word finding, vomiting, right arm twitching · right hemiparesis → lung primary
tx: 2 · then radiation: whole-brain or stereotactic radiosurgery
~ choice depends on clinical status, prognosis
steroids, anti-seizure drug · resected even though lung biopsy possible (symptomatic) · brain + chest radiation · died at 14 months

head: h
High-grade glioma
grade 3 anaplastic · grade 4 glioblastoma
pres: headache, confusion, memory loss · normal exam → MRI: deep glioblastoma → steroids, stereotactic biopsy, palliative radiation + chemo · died at 5 months
tx: ~ resecting all visible tumour helps, but NOT curative
~ worse with age, poor performance status
• early: neuro worsening, hair loss, dermatitis, otitis externa, fatigue
• late: cognitive decline, focal necrosis, radiation vasculitis (stroke), second cancer

head: h
Low-grade glioma
grade 2 · slow, but still MALIGNANT
only grade 1 (pilocytic astrocytoma) is not
pres: first tonic-clonic seizure, no headache → non-enhancing glioma · seizure-free on anti-seizure drugs
tx: • clear progression on MRI (starts to enhance)

head: h
Primary CNS lymphoma
non-neural tissue, confined to the CNS
NOT spread from systemic lymphoma
rising incidence
tx: biopsy, as for every brain tumour

head: h
Raised intracranial pressure
Monro-Kellie: rigid skull
brain + CSF + blood + mass
pres: ~ compensates only up to a point

head: h
Herniation
Cushing triad:
hypertension, bradycardia, apnea
pres: • ipsilateral CN III palsy + dilated pupil

head: h
Paraneoplastic syndromes
rare: 0.01% of cancers
PRECEDES the cancer by weeks to months
